title: Disulfide-poly(β-amino ester) nanoparticles for glutathione-responsive drug delivery
content: Stimuli-responsive polymeric nanocarriers have emerged as promising platforms for controlled drug delivery, enabling cargo release in response to specific biological signals. Among triggers, the high intracellular concentration of glutathione (GSH) offers a unique opportunity to activate redox-responsive systems through cleavage of disulfide bonds. In this work, a disulfide-containing poly(β-amino ester) (PBAE) was synthesized and conjugated with PEG to obtain block copolymers capable of spontaneous self-assembly into polymeric nanoparticles. While PBAEs have been previously established for nucleic acid delivery, their application as redox-responsive drug carriers for the physical encapsulation of small-molecule therapeutics remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that a disulfide-containing PEG–PBAE copolymer can efficiently encapsulate punicalagin (a model drug) through self-assembly, forming nanoparticles with hydrodynamic diameters below 200 nm and a near-neutral ζ-potential. These nanosystems showed pronounced redox-responsive behavior, with sustained drug release in the presence of GSH while limited release under physiological conditions (ca. 10%). The nanoparticles also exhibited good cytocompatibility at concentrations up to 0.2 mg mL−1. Overall, this study investigates the potential of combining the versatility of PBAEs with disulfide-mediated responsiveness to develop polymeric nanocarriers for controlled glutathione-triggered small-molecule drug release.
